what_its_for: Trimethobenzamide is used to treat nausea and vomiting. It works by blocking signals in the brain that cause you to feel sick to your stomach.
how_to_take: Trimethobenzamide comes as a capsule you swallow by mouth. Take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 300 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, as needed. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well your kidneys work or how severe your nausea is. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you still feel nauseous, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store trimethobenzamide capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially sedatives, sleep aids, anxiety medications, or antihistamines, as combining these with trimethobenzamide can cause increased drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: uncontrolled muscle movements or spasms (especially in your face, neck, or arms), severe dizziness or fainting, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), high fever, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, or if your nausea and vomiting do not improve or get worse after taking this medication.
when_it_works: Trimethobenzamide usually starts working within 30 to 45 minutes after you take it. The effects typically last for 3 to 4 hours. If your symptoms do not improve within a reasonable time, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older) may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and drowsiness, so use with caution and follow your doctor's guidance. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. This medication is not recommended for use in children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication, as safety has not been fully established in these situations.
